The undead are tough creatures, each having already survived death at least once. Warlocks who make a pact\s
with Undead will find themselves gaining additional resistances such as cold, poison, darkness and\s
nether. In addition, they will be able to see invisible monsters and gain resistance to\s
life-draining forces. They will also gain access to undeadly powers, which typically\s
involve detection and control over the forces of the netherworld. Eventually, this pact will allow\s
its practitioners to destroy monsters with a single word, and, perhaps, to even partially leave\s
the world of the living altogether. Of course, allying with the undead substantially reduces the\s
warlock's ability to fight these creatures.
Molto allegro. A song of defiance, its melody captures the essence of\s
the dragon's lust for treasure and conquest. Woe be to all that hear\s
this ancient dragon song.
The bond between a Dragonrider and a Dragon is one of the strongest and most enduring ties\s
seen the world over. Each draws strength, power, and encouragement from the other, and together\s
they make a formidable foe. An alliance with Dragonkind enables this bond to form, and the Warlock\s
of this pact gains impressive powers for mounted combat. Indeed, they are among the elite riders\s
of the world, only slightly inferior to Cavalry and Beastmasters. But where they have a slight\s
deficiency in skill (and perhaps in melee as well), they have a strong advantage in riding techniques\s
and magical enhancements. Dragonriders favor the lance above all other weapons, and seek continuously\s
the legendary 'Dragonlance' which they view as their long-lost birthright.
Angels are heavenly beings who use a variety of techniques to smite those they view as evil.\s
Warlocks who make pacts with Angels will also find their saving throws significantly improved,\s
and (eventually) their body almost immune to bolt-like effects. Since Angels are strongly aligned\s
with the forces of good, making a pact with Angels will reduce damage done to all good monsters\s
by a substantial amount.
Demons are crafty creatures of Hell, using whatever means at their disposal to bring\s
down their enemies. Warlocks who make pacts with Demons will find their abilities to use\s
all magical devices improved, and learn the ability to Recharge these devices at will.\s
Eventually, Demon Warlocks attain the ability to crush walls beneath their footsteps, and\s
even gain immunity to fire. Making a pact with Demons will reduce damage done to all demons by a substantial amount.
An alliance with hounds is sneakily strong: hounds are fast, stealthy and nimble,\s
and the warlock will gain these attributes as well, in addition to basic elemental\s
resistances. They also gain decent melee, and the ability to channel the unpredictable\s
powers of the aether. Of course, Hound Warlocks may also call on their kin for assistance,\s
though this may not be enough against the more difficult foes of the world. Still, wouldn't\s
it be fun to have some of those annoying hounds on your side for a change?
Of all the icky, crawling things in the world, you have chosen to make an alliance\s
with spiders? Sure, they are stealthy, and fast, and very adept at hiding. Able\s
to extrude a fine sticky substance to ensnare the unwary, the spider lurks nearby,\s
or so you assume since you very seldom see them. Moreover, many spiders are adept at\s
the powers of teleportation, able to jump quickly from one location to another, which\s
can be quite baffling to a would be predator. They are comfortable with both poison\s
and nexus. They are a bit on the squishy side, though - that is, if you\s
manage to catch one!
An alliance with giants and titans grants impressive physical strength and fortitude,\s
but other stats will generally suffer. Later in life, you will gain giant-like resistances\s
including sound, shards and chaos. Your combat will be impressive; and like giants, you\s
will favor heavy weapons. Oh, and you won't mind tossing a boulder or two should the need\s
arise! This alliance offers much in the way of physical advantages, but very\s
little in the way of magical abilities or skill. Warlocks with this alliance are\s
excellent fighters, being nearly indistiguishable in skill from Warriors!
Warlocks are a magical class; they derive their spells and powers not from books,\s
but from an eldritch pact made with a given class of monsters. This pact is irrevocable\s
and is made at the outset of the Warlock's career. Depending on the class of monsters with whom\s
they ally, the warlock will gain unique bonuses, abilities and magical powers; for example,\s
alliance with the forces of the netherworld grants resistances to poison and nether, enhanced\s
constitution and spells to control and conjure the unliving, as well as spells to access\s
the damaging forces of the netherworld directly. Each such alliance has thematic bonuses\s
and powers, and you can read the details in the respective help sections.\n\n
Allying with a given class of monsters dramatically reduces the warlock's ability to fight\s
these foes. Instead, the warlock seeks cooperation with their brethren, or perhaps domination\s
over them; direct assaults are rarely successful.\n \n
In addition to pact-related spells, all warlocks gain access to the unique power of the\s
Eldritch Blast. Their primary spell stat is Charisma, since they seek dominion and alliance\s
with their chosen kin, and these monsters tend to have a strong will of their own.
A Warrior is a hack-and-slash character, who solves most of his\s
problems by cutting them to pieces, but will occasionally fall\s
back on the help of a magical device. Unfortunately, many\s
high-level devices may be forever beyond their use.\n \n
Warriors cast no spells. They hate magic. In fact, they even\s
gain experience for destroying high level spellbooks. They have a\s
class power - 'Sword Dancing' - which allows them to conduct a\s
melee attack in six random directions.
A Warrior-Mage is precisely what the name suggests: a cross\s
between a warrior and a mage. To support their good-for-mages combat\s
abilities, Warrior-Mages begin the game with Arcane magic and can\s
freely select another spell realm. Although they do not gain\s
new spells as fast as regular mages, they can eventually learn\s
all or almost all spells in both realms, making them a very competitive\s
choice for those who appreciate Arcane magic. Their class powers\s
allow them to convert either HP to mana, or mana to HP, as needed.
The mighty axe! Your blows will cleave with damage unsurpassed.\s
Specializing in axes gives great offensive prowess, especially when\s
your axe is wielded with two hands. However, this speciality offers\s
little in the way of utility. Kill quickly as your life depends on it!
You will shoot to kill! The bowmaster gains techniques to enhance shooting,\s
including more rapid firing, the ability to volley shots over the heads of\s
intervening monsters, reduced ammo destruction, the ability to kill with a\s
single arrow and much more. As a shooter, your missile prowess will be quite\s
formidable, though your melee will be somewhat lacking.
You will seek to club your opponents senseless! This speciality gains passive\s
status effects against monsters, such as confusion, knock out and stunning. Also,\s
you will gain some limited utility techniques. At high levels, your weapons will\s
become more likely to score devastating, crushing blows against your hapless enemies.
The crossbowmaster shoots deadly bolts for great damage. Their bolts may explode\s
powerfully damaging nearby monsters. Also, they may shoot so hard as to knock\s
their opponents backwards!
A knife in the back! This speciality favors dual-wielding and rogue-type behavior.\s
The daggermaster can even assume the posture of The Flying Dagger which greatly\s
enhances their low level dagger toss capability. Indeed, their prowess with the\s
dagger toss is legendary and appears almost magical! At high levels, you will also\s
gain formidable melee prowess with the Frenzy Stance. Finally, daggermasters have\s
very strong short ranged teleport techniques that synergize well with their toss\s
You don a grim face before setting out to reap your harvest of death. You will swing\s
your weapon wide often affecting multiple surrounding opponents.
Specializing in shields gives excellent powers of defense and retaliation. In addition,\s
you can even choose to melee with your shield rather than a normal weapon, bashing your\s
opponents senseless. This form of combat is known as Shield Bashing and is unique to this\s
Watch out, Goliath! As a master of slings you will shoot pebbles with uncanny speed. Your\s
shots may even ricochet off other monsters to score multiple hits. As with other archery\s
specializations, your ammo will break less often.
Monkey King! You will battle opponents with a flurry of blows from your mighty\s
staff and will be prepared to counter the attacks of your enemies. You can vault into\s
battle and circle kick enemies for stunning effects, attacking them with your boots!\s
You may even eventually clone yourself at great cost.
You will become a true swordmaster! Mastery of the blade will augment\s
your weapon with elemental, vorpal or vampiric powers.
A master of digging. You prefer rocky enclosures and don't mind\s
lugging around a corpse or two, which you can bury in a pinch for\s
a temporary bonus. You can choose one of several postures which allow\s
you to use the digging bonus of your current weapon as an additional\s
bonus, such as increased strength, constitution, or even speed! So keep\s
your eye open for those +8 diggers!
A Weaponmaster is exceptionally good with a single class of weapons,\s
obtaining special combat bonuses and powers which depend on their chosen\s
speciality. Focus is the key to success; weaponmasters are truly lousy\s
with off-speciality weapons, but few can match the prowess they gain\s
with something more suitable in their hands.
A Weaponsmith can improve weapons and armors for him or herself.\s
They are good at fighting, and they have potential ability to\s
become even better than Warriors using improved equipment. They\s
cannot cast spells, and are poor at skills such as stealth or\s
magic defense.\n \n
A Weaponsmith extracts the essences of special effects from weapons\s
or armors which have various special abilities, and can add these\s
essences to another weapon or armor. Normally, each equipment can\s
be improved only once, but they can remove a previously added\s
essence from improved equipment to improve it with another\s
essence. To-hit, to-damage bonus, and AC can be improved freely\s
up to a maximum value depending on level. Weaponsmiths use class\s
powers for Smithing commands.
Werewolves are fearsome hunters who can assume either human or wolf shape.\s
They are exceptionally durable in both forms, and have great powers of\s
regeneration, though they are infamously vulnerable to fire and silver,\s
and are not particularly good at using magical spells or devices in either\s
shape. While in wolf form, werewolves wield no weapons; instead, they\s
attack with their teeth and claws. As werewolves wear different equipment\s
in human form and wolf form, they use one inventory slot for a special\s
satchel in which they keep the items not needed in their current shape.
Wild-Talents gain random talents and abilities as they\s
level up. They are good fighters, and decent with magical devices,\s
but their true forte is their vast array of potential random\s
powers. Except you never know what those might be!\n \n
Wild-Talents do not have a spell stat. Instead, each ability that\s
they gain requires its own individual stat for the purposes of fail rate\s
calculation; for example, Tossing a Boulder requires Strength,\s
while Magic Missile requires Intelligence. Each spell requires mana\s
to cast, but the amount of mana available is not influenced by any\s
particular stat and is determined simply by experience.
A Yellow-Mage is a type of Mage who focuses on rapid spell casting.\s
The casting speed of Yellow-Mages improves with experience; low-level spells\s
are particularly quick to use, and can eventually be cast as many as five\s
times in one round! But even a level 50 spell requires less than half a\s
turn for an accomplished Yellow-Mage.\n\n
In most other respects, a Yellow-Mage is similar to a Mage; they use Intelligence\s
as their primary spell stat, and may learn spells from two spell realms of their choice.\s
However, due to their focus on hasty casting, some of the deepest\s
and most powerful magic will remain forever beyond their grasp.
Disciples of Yeqrezh can choose five special gifts, one every ten levels.\s
These gifts can take the form of new abilities, physical powers, or rare items;\s
some can be chosen repeatedly, while others can only be picked once.\s
Once you have selected a gift, you can never go back on your decision, so you\s
might want to study this list to decide which gifts to choose for your character.\n\n
Yeqrezh is the friendliest of the Purples, supportive of his Disciples\s
and willing to let them find their own way. Disciples of Yeqrezh will\s
learn 20 spells over the course of the game - one every two character\s
levels, apart from levels 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50; seventeen of these\s
spells are offered by Yeqrezh, while the other three (at levels 16,\s
32 and 48) are chosen by you. Every ten levels, Yeqrezh offers direct\s
help to his Disciples; depending on your choice, he can give you rare\s
items or a permanent mental or physical ability, or share some of his\s
life experience with you. Some of these abilities can be improved\s
repeatedly, allowing you to accumulate exceptional mastery.\n\n
Disciples of Yeqrezh gain many practical tools as well as solid offensive\s
options, and a useful item as a gift from their patron every odd-numbered\s
character level. They are the most mage-like of all Disciples, and lack of\s
hit points is their only true weakness. Nevertheless, they are extremely\s
versatile, and can also win through melee, archery or even sneaking about\s
silently collecting loot.\n\n
Yeqrezh is the recommended patron for new (or highly cautious) players, as he\s
is the only Purple not to actively incentivize a demanding, push-the-envelope\s
approach. Yeqrezh's disciples, like Karrot's, rely on Intelligence to\s
power their spells.
